tasks.short: Stay current in physical science fields

steps.what: Define literature topics, sources and search criteria for current developments
Retrieve current literature matches from the saved source queries
Read current literature, discuss developments with colleagues and participate in professional conferences

tasks.design: Configure native catalogue and journal alerts delivered through {EMAIL}, retaining useful links in {DOCS}. The lecturer still reads papers, evaluates methods, discusses ideas and attends conferences; retrieval does not replace learning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated source searches compete with reading and professional discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing literature catalogues and journal services support saved searches and alerts.
tasks.still_hard: Recognize important results and assess relevance across scientific subfields.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate new evidence with disciplinary understanding.

ambition.what: Notice relevant new publications between regular literature review sessions.

tasks.altitude: Choose coverage deliberately while protecting substantive reading and discussion.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI supplies topic summaries and foundational papers; this supports literature discovery, not replacement of critical reading or measured savings here.
Native saved searches and alerts can remove repeated retrieval; the proposed time effect is model knowledge.

assumptions: The lecturer produces topic terms, synonyms, source list, date window, exclusion terms and delivery frequency in s1; its 10 hours includes query capture and initial recall checks.
Source catalogues produce linked publication matches from those definitions; missing coverage returns to manual search and reading in s3.
Configure native alerts before adding a summarization or crawling service.
Four extra focal hours per 100 baseline hours cover query changes and coverage checks.
Conference attendance and colleague discussion retain full time; source access already automated today earns no new saving.
research_questions: Do saved searches reduce repeated retrieval without adding screening noise or missing important papers?

already_counted.description: Reading, critical appraisal and professional participation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85; gross 15 minus 4 upkeep gives central net 11%. Range 0-5% allows screening noise and uncertain retrieval share; existing alerts save zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold office hours for student assistance

steps.what: Maintain scheduled office hours and assist students with course questions and learning difficulties

tasks.design: Retain scheduled student assistance using {CALENDAR} and course material in {LMS}. The lecturer explains concepts and explores difficulties; a booking feature does not remove the office-hour commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Students need context-sensitive explanation and a chance to ask follow-up questions.
tasks.still_hard: Recognize the misunderstanding behind the question.

reach.task: Help students work through conceptual difficulties

evidence.claim: Office-hour teaching and student assistance retain full time in this design.

assumptions: This task owns course-related assistance and the scheduled availability commitment.
Curriculum and career advice is allocated to the separate advising task; the same minutes must be assigned once in a role roll-up.
No separate scheduling administration baseline is invented.
Use existing calendar and learning materials with no new automation upkeep.
unknowns: Office-hour arrangements and student support needs
research_questions: Is there a separate repeated coordination burden beyond the scheduled availability and assistance?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Scheduled availability and actual student help remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise students on curricula and careers

steps.what: Advise students on curriculum choices and career issues through individualized discussion

tasks.design: The lecturer uses current curriculum information in {DOCS} to discuss options with the student. Advice stays personal and qualified; no automatic recommendation or inferred student eligibility is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Choices depend on goals, constraints and uncertain future opportunities.
tasks.still_hard: Help the student weigh trade-offs without overpromising career outcomes.
tasks.human_edge: Listen, ask useful questions and understand individual preferences.
tasks.altitude: Own thoughtful academic and vocational guidance.

evidence.claim: Individual academic and career guidance retains its discussion and judgement time.

assumptions: This task owns curriculum and career advice wherever it occurs; course troubleshooting belongs to office-hour assistance and shared minutes are assigned once.
No large repeated data-entry stage is assumed inside advising.
Existing curriculum documents remain with no new tool or upkeep.
unknowns: Student advising responsibilities and specialist referral options
research_questions: Which factual lookups recur separately from required personal discussion?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Individual discussion and contextual advice remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate on teaching and research issues

steps.what: Collaborate with colleagues to understand and resolve teaching and research issues

tasks.design: Keep collaborative interpretation and agreement with colleagues using {DOCS} and {CHAT}. No large minutes-production or administrative baseline is assumed merely because the collaboration happens in meetings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Issues require different expertise and agreement among colleagues.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared documents support joint deliberation.
tasks.still_hard: Reconcile conflicting interpretations and choose feasible next steps.
tasks.human_edge: Contribute expertise and build mutual understanding.
tasks.altitude: Own useful contributions to collective teaching and research decisions.

evidence.claim: Teaching and research collaboration retains human deliberation time in this design.

assumptions: The baseline is substantive collaboration rather than a separate meeting-administration process.
Existing shared documents and chat suffice, with no new automation maintenance.
unknowns: Collaboration format and recurrent administrative burdens
research_questions: Is there repeated evidence assembly that can be separated from substantive collaborative discussion?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Collaboration and agreement retain full time.

role.altitude: Choose literature coverage deliberately while protecting student support and academic collaboration.
reach: Work with librarians on search coverage
Support interdisciplinary teaching with environmental science colleagues
role.ambitious_version: A science lecturer who automates repeated literature retrieval while retaining critical reading, student assistance, career guidance and colleague deliberation.
